lessons.title: Flags
intro: After almost every instruction, the 6502 sets a few one-bit flags that describe the result. You already know the carry (C). Two more matter all the time.
Z, the zero flag, is 1 when the result was exactly $00. N, the negative flag, is 1 when the result is $80 or more (its highest bit is set). Programmers use $80 to $FF as negative numbers.
LDA, LDX, LDY, INX, DEX, ADC, SBC and the transfers all set Z and N. STA, STX and STY never touch the flags. On the board, every flag has its own little LED.

exercises.prompt: What is the Z flag after LDA #0?
exercises.explanation: The result is $00, so the zero flag is set to 1.

exercises.prompt: What is the Z flag after this program?
exercises.explanation: DEX makes X 2, which isn't zero, so Z is 0.

exercises.prompt: Which values set the N flag?
exercises.explanation: N copies the highest bit of the result. That bit is 1 for $80 and everything above.

exercises.prompt: What do N and Z show after LDA #$90?
exercises.explanation: $90 is $80 or more, so N = 1. It isn't zero, so Z = 0.

exercises.prompt: Which instruction never changes the flags?
exercises.explanation: Storing doesn't create a new result, so STA, STX and STY leave all flags alone.

exercises.prompt: Count X down to zero, so that the Z flag gets set.
exercises.explanation: DEX turns 1 into 0 and sets Z. INX would make it 2.

lessons.title: Branches and Labels
intro: Flags become useful when the program reacts to them. A branch jumps to another place in the program, but only if a flag is set a certain way.
BEQ (Branch if EQual) jumps when Z = 1, so when the last result was zero. BNE (Branch if Not Equal) jumps when Z = 0. If the branch doesn't jump, the program simply continues with the next line.
Where to? To a label: a name followed by a colon, like DONE: or ZERO:. The assembler works out the address for you.

exercises.prompt: A is 5 now. What is X at the end?
exercises.explanation: LDA #5 isn't zero, so Z = 0 and BEQ doesn't jump. LDX #1 runs, then BRK.

options: A name for a place in the program
A memory address you have to calculate yourself
exercises.explanation: Labels like LOOP: or DONE: name a line. Branches and jumps use the name, the assembler fills in the address.

exercises.prompt: Jump to SKIP when the result was not zero.
exercises.explanation: BNE jumps when Z = 0, so when the value wasn't zero.

exercises.prompt: This program should store 1 at $0300 only when A is 0. But with A = 5 it still stores 1. Which line is wrong?
exercises.explanation: We want to skip the store when A is not zero. That's BNE. BEQ skips it in exactly the wrong case.

exercises.prompt: What happens at a BNE when the Z flag is 1?
options: Nothing, the program continues with the next line
It jumps back to the start
exercises.explanation: A branch only jumps when its condition is true. BNE needs Z = 0.

exercises.prompt: Build a program that ends with X = 2.
exercises.explanation: A is 0, so BEQ jumps over LDX #1 to the label TWO.

lessons.title: More Branches
intro: JMP LABEL always jumps, no flag needed. Use it to skip over code or to go back to the start of something.
There are branches for the other flags too: BCS (Carry Set) and BCC (Carry Clear) check the carry, BMI (MInus) and BPL (PLus) check the N flag.
Branches can only jump about 127 bytes forward or backward, because they store the distance in one byte. If the assembler says BRANCH TOO FAR, use a JMP instead.

output: X = $01 (the sum didn't fit, so the carry was set)

exercises.explanation: JMP doesn't look at any flag. The B… instructions only jump when their flag condition is true.

exercises.prompt: What is X at the end?
exercises.explanation: $F0 is $80 or more, so N = 1 and BMI jumps to NEG.

exercises.prompt: Jump to OK when the carry is clear.
exercises.explanation: BCC = Branch if Carry Clear. 10 + 20 fits in a byte, so the carry stays 0 and it jumps.

exercises.prompt: The assembler says ?BRANCH TOO FAR. What do you do?
options: Use JMP for the long jump
exercises.explanation: Branches only reach about 127 bytes. JMP can reach any address.

exercises.prompt: This program never stops. Which line causes it?
exercises.explanation: JMP LOOP always jumps back, so the program never reaches BRK.
